title: International university student (campus info desk, 4 classes, Canvas, evening crammer, first-gen) ate out with cousins: the card showed $40.00 pending, the slip had a tip, and the charge posted Friday as $48.00; Dev reads the one charge, finds no duplicate or error, and stays quiet.

changes.content: Dinner with my cousins on Wednesday: the card showed $40.00 pending, I added a tip on the slip.

best_fix.what: Nothing. Dev replaces the pending $40.00 with the posted $48.00 at Riverside Grill (x-dinner, authorized Wed Nov 25, posted Fri Nov 27), keeps one charge, and says nothing. If she opens the card: 'That's the $40.00 plus your $8.00 tip.' Available now stays $1,046.54 and its bills before the next paycheck are covered.
best_fix.why: She told Dev herself (m-receipt) that she added a tip on the slip, so $48.00 is expected and not a duplicate, a wrong amount or a fee. The pending amount no longer exists, so nothing is counted twice. Her Nov 27 paycheck ($303.84) is already in; the next bill is the $75.00 transit pass on Dec 1 and nothing needs moving.

must_not: flag the Riverside Grill charge as a duplicate, an overcharge or a dispute (x-dinner is $40.00 plus her tip)
count both the $40.00 pending and the $48.00 posted amounts
ask her to log or confirm the tip (m-receipt already says it)
send a card or push about the charge on Saturday morning, during her family call (m-02)
tell her to cut back on eating out
send a card or push about the Riverside Grill charge being $8.00 more than the pending amount on Saturday morning
assumptions: Restaurants often add the tip when the charge posts; the bank shows the final amount two days after the card authorization.
The simulator posts the dinner on Fri Nov 27 with authorized date Wed Nov 25; the pending $40.00 itself exists only in what she told Dev (m-receipt).
Her Nov 27 paycheck of $303.84 is already in checking and is counted because it has landed.

tempting.suggestion: send a card or push about the Riverside Grill charge being $8.00 more than the pending amount on Saturday morning
tempting.why_wrong: Saturday 9:00 to 9:45 AM is her firm weekly call with family, and the difference is the tip she already told Dev about
